Job Description

Position: Associate Manager of Education and Outreach

Location: Denver, CO (Hybrid)

Salary Range: $60,000–$90,000, commensurate with experience

Application Deadline: Rolling until filled

Apply at: www.tinyurl.com/ApplyForMI

About the Mizel Museum

The Mizel Museum is a nonprofit educational organization dedicated to fostering cross-cultural understanding through educational programs, cultural experiences, and community engagement. The Museum inspires learners of all ages to explore Holocaust education, cultural identity, history, and the shared responsibility of building more inclusive communities. We are a collaborative team of mission-driven professionals committed to building inclusive communities through education. We offer competitive wages, excellent benefits, professional growth opportunities, and a welcoming, purpose-driven work environment.

About the Role

Inspire the next generation through education. The Mizel Museum is seeking an experienced educator who is passionate about helping students build empathy, critical thinking, and cross-cultural understanding. If you love teaching but are looking for an opportunity to make an impact beyond the traditional classroom, we’d love to meet you. Current and former classroom teachers, instructional coaches, and school-based educators are especially encouraged to apply.

The Education & Outreach Associate Manager serves as one of the Museum’s primary educators and ambassadors, helping connect thousands of students, teachers, and community members each year with meaningful educational experiences focused on Holocaust education, cross-cultural understanding, and social justice.

This role combines education, relationship-building, and program coordination. The Associate Manager works closely with schools to schedule educational programs, delivers engaging in-person and virtual instruction, builds lasting relationships with educators, and helps ensure programs continue to grow in quality, reach, and impact.

The ideal candidate is an experienced educator who enjoys working with students, collaborating with teachers, and creating engaging learning experiences. They are equally comfortable teaching in a classroom, presenting virtually, or representing the Museum at community events. They are curious, adaptable, and excited to help shape the future of museum education.

What You’ll Do

School & Community Engagement (35%)

Build and strengthen relationships with educators, schools, and community organizations while expanding participation in Museum educational programming.

• Cultivate and maintain relationships throughout Colorado.

• Conduct outreach to schools and educational partners to increase participation.

• Schedule and coordinate in-person and virtual educational programs.

• Respond to educator inquiries and provide outstanding customer service throughout the scheduling process.

• Represent the Museum at school visits, conferences, educator events, and community outreach opportunities.

• Identify opportunities to expand the Museum’s educational reach and strengthen long-term partnerships.

Educational Program Delivery (35%)

Deliver engaging educational experiences that inspire students and support educators.

• Facilitate Holocaust education, cross-cultural understanding, and social justice programs for K–12 students and community audiences.

• Teach both virtual and in-person educational programs using engaging, age-appropriate instructional strategies.

• Adapt presentations to meet the developmental needs of elementary, middle, and high school audiences.

• Create positive, inclusive, and engaging learning environments.

• Serve as a knowledgeable and professional ambassador for the Museum’s educational mission.

• Support evaluation efforts by gathering participant and educator feedback.

Program Coordination & Support (15%)

Support the successful planning and execution of Museum educational programming.

• Coordinate program logistics, materials, scheduling, and classroom resources.

• Maintain accurate program records, attendance, and educational reporting.

• Collaborate with Marketing & Communications to support program promotion.

• Partner with Operations to ensure educational programs are well organized and successfully executed.

• Assist with occasional evening, weekend, and community events.

Program Development & Continuous Improvement (15%)

Help strengthen and expand the Museum’s educational offerings.

• Provide feedback and ideas to improve existing educational programs.

• Assist with the development of new educational initiatives and curriculum enhancements.

• Stay informed on current educational best practices, instructional strategies, and Colorado Academic Standards.

• Analyze educator feedback and participation trends to recommend program improvements.

• Leverage technology, AI-powered tools, and emerging educational resources to improve lesson preparation, educational materials, workflow efficiency, and participant engagement.

Success in the Role

A successful Education & Outreach Associate Manager will build strong relationships with educators and schools, consistently deliver engaging educational experiences, expand participation in Museum programs, contribute to the continued growth of Holocaust and cross-cultural education initiatives, and help ensure every educator and student has a meaningful learning experience. They will continually seek opportunities to improve programming, strengthen educational partnerships, and leverage technology and AI-enabled tools to enhance teaching, outreach, and organizational effectiveness.

Required Qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree in Education, History, Social Studies, Museum Studies, Public History, Communications, or experience in a related field.

• Minimum of 3 years of experience teaching, facilitating, or delivering educational programming.

• Experience managing classrooms, student groups, or educational learning environments.

• Demonstrated ability to build relationships with educators, schools, and community organizations.

• Excellent presentation, facilitation, and verbal communication skills.

• Strong written communication and organizational skills.

• Ability to adapt instruction for diverse age groups, learning styles, and educational settings.

• Strong customer service orientation and a professional, collaborative approach to working with educators, students, and community partners.

• Ability to manage multiple priorities while maintaining exceptional attention to detail.

• Comfort learning and utilizing new technology platforms, virtual presentation tools, and educational software.

• Ability to work independently and collaboratively.

• Ability to work occasional evenings and weekends.

Preferred Qualifications

• Current or former classroom teacher, instructional coach, or educational specialist.

• Teaching license or previous teaching certification.

• Experience with Holocaust education, multicultural education, civics, history, social studies, or social justice education.

• Experience developing or adapting educational curriculum and lesson plans.

• Experience presenting in both virtual and in-person learning environments.

• Existing relationships within Colorado school districts or educational organizations.

• Experience using AI-powered and emerging technology tools to support lesson planning, educational research, presentation development, program evaluation, workflow efficiency, and educational innovation.

• Spanish language proficiency is a plus but not required.

Work Authorization

Candidates must be legally authorized to work in the United States at the time of application and throughout employment. The Mizel Museum does not provide employment visa sponsorship now or in the future.

About Adam’s Purpose

Adam’s Purpose is a nonprofit organization dedicated to providing help, hope, and healing to bereaved Black mothers and mothers of Color and their families following pregnancy and infant loss or the death of a child, adolescent, or adult child . Recognizing that the loss of a child profoundly affects the entire family, we provide support that honors the interconnected healing needs of mothers, fathers and caregivers, surviving siblings, and loved ones.

Through culturally responsive, grief- and trauma-informed, healing-centered care , specialized grief and behavioral health services, peer support, healing circles, education, advocacy, and community partnerships, Adam’s Purpose is expanding equitable access to compassionate, high-quality grief care while reducing disparities experienced by bereaved families.

Contract Term: Initial six (6) month contract with the possibility of renewal based on organizational needs, participant demand, funding availability, performance, credentialing status, and mutual agreement.

Reports To: Executive Director & Founder

Position Summary

Adam’s Purpose is seeking a compassionate, independently licensed therapist to provide specialized grief and behavioral health services for bereaved Black mothers, mothers of Color, and their families. This contractor will deliver evidence-based, culturally responsive, grief- and trauma-informed, healing-centered care through individual, family, and group therapy while supporting the continued development of Adam’s Purpose’s specialized clinical services.

The therapist will utilize SimplePractice for clinical documentation and participate in the organization’s Medicaid and commercial insurance readiness by maintaining high-quality documentation that supports medical necessity, quality care, and reimbursement.

Essential Responsibilities

Clinical Services

Conduct comprehensive behavioral health assessments and diagnostic evaluations.

Develop individualized treatment plans and establish DSM-5 diagnoses, when clinically appropriate.

Provide individual, family, and group therapy utilizing evidence-based grief and trauma interventions.

Deliver grief counseling, trauma treatment, crisis intervention, safety planning, and psychoeducation.

Administer and interpret appropriate clinical screening and outcome measures.

Coordinate referrals and collaborate with community providers to ensure continuity of care.

Support whole-family healing by engaging fathers and caregivers, surviving siblings, and other family members as clinically appropriate.

Group Facilitation

Facilitate or co-facilitate Adam’s Purpose support groups and healing programs, including Angel Moms, A Mother’s Mourn, Family Healing Circles, and other grief-focused programming.

Collaborate with Peer Advocates to provide integrated therapeutic and peer support services.

Documentation & Electronic Health Record

Utilize Adam’s Purpose’s SimplePractice electronic health record (EHR) for scheduling, telehealth, treatment planning, progress notes, secure messaging, and clinical documentation.

Complete documentation accurately and within organizational timelines.

Maintain participant records in accordance with HIPAA, professional ethics, organizational policies, and payer requirements.

Insurance Credentialing & Compliance

Participate in Medicaid and commercial insurance credentialing, enrollment, and recredentialing activities as requested.

Complete documentation that supports medical necessity and reimbursement.

Collaborate with Adam’s Purpose and contracted billing partners to resolve documentation questions related to claims or authorizations.

Participate in quality improvement, chart reviews, and clinical consultation as requested.

Collaboration

Work collaboratively with the Executive Director & Founder, Case Manager, Peer Advocates, contracted clinical consultants, and community partners to provide coordinated, participant-centered care.

Required Qualifications

Active, unrestricted Colorado independent clinical license as an LCSW, LPC, LMFT, or Licensed Psychologist , with eligibility to participate in Medicaid and commercial insurance credentialing through Adam’s Purpose.

Minimum of two (2) years of post-licensure clinical experience.

Experience providing grief, trauma, and behavioral health services.

Commitment to culturally responsive, grief- and trauma-informed, healing-centered care.

Strong clinical assessment, documentation, communication, and organizational skills.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience serving bereaved Black mothers, mothers of Color, and families impacted by pregnancy and infant loss or the death of a child, adolescent, or adult child.

Experience facilitating grief support groups.

Current Colorado Medicaid and/or commercial insurance credentialing.

Experience with Medicaid documentation and reimbursement requirements.

Experience utilizing SimplePractice or another behavioral health EHR.

Experience providing telehealth services.

Bilingual or multilingual candidates are encouraged to apply.

Physical Requirements

Ability to provide services in person, virtually, and in occasional community-based settings.

Ability to travel throughout the Denver Metro area as needed.

Ability to maintain participant confidentiality and exercise sound clinical judgment.

Background Screening

Selected contractors must successfully complete a criminal background check and verification of professional licensure, education, credentials, and professional liability insurance.

Equal Opportunity Employer

Adam’s Purpose is committed to fostering a diverse, equitable, and inclusive workplace. We encourage applications from individuals with diverse backgrounds and lived experiences who are passionate about advancing equitable access to specialized grief and behavioral health services.

Summary

In this position, you will be a key member of the Energy Policy Team, reporting to the Lead Energy Policy Administrator. You will be a key contributor to the team’s advocacy at the Colorado Public Utilities Commission (PUC), support its engagement on state and local legislative matters, and represent the city across a range of stakeholders.

Description

About Our Job

With competitive pay, great benefits, and endless opportunities, working for the City and County of Denver means seeing yourself working with purpose — for you, and those who benefit from your passion, skills and expertise. Join our diverse, inclusive and talented workforce of more than 11,000 team members who are at the heart of what makes Denver, Denver.

What We Offer

The City and County of Denver offers a competitive salary commensurate with education and experience. The salary range for this position is $90,000.00 – $115,000.00. We also offer generous benefits for full-time employees which include but are not limited to:

A guaranteed life-long monthly pension, once vested after 5 years of service

457B Retirement Plan

140 hours of PTO earned within first year + 12 paid holidays, 1 personal holiday, 1 Wellness Day, and 1 volunteer day per year

Competitive medical, dental and vision plans effective within 1 month of start date

Location

The City and County of Denver supports a hybrid workplace model. Employees work where needed, at a job site 3 days per week and off-site as needed. The Office of Climate Action, Sustainability and Resiliency requires 3 days in office at the Wellington Webb Municipal Building, located at 201 W. Colfax Ave., Denver, CO 80202. Employees must work within the state of Colorado on their off-site days.

What You’ll Do

The Office of Climate Action, Sustainability and Resiliency’s (CASR) vision is to build a carbon pollution-free, sustainable, and resilient Denver for all. Guided by science and shaped by community input, CASR delivers bold solutions through policies, programs, and capital projects that reduce emissions, advance environmental justice, and strengthen climate resilience. Our portfolio includes beneficial electrification, energy efficiency, renewable energy, energy storage, climate adaptation, community resilience, nature-based solutions, natural resource conservation, embodied carbon, waste reduction and diversion, communications, community engagement, and workforce development—all with a strong focus on equity. This work is driving measurable progress toward a healthier, more sustainable Denver for generations to come.

CASR’s Energy Policy Team is housed within the Climate Action Division, which works to equitably meet Denver’s energy and transportation needs with affordable, reliable, and carbon-free systems. The team is focused on advancing meaningful decarbonization policies through advocacy before state regulatory authorities and partnership with the city’s energy utility provider. Success requires active coordination across CASR, other city agencies, and city leadership — in addition to engagement with partner organizations and an array of stakeholder groups.

CASR is looking to fill two positions as Senior Energy Policy Advisor. In this position, you will be a key member of the Energy Policy Team, reporting to the Lead Energy Policy Administrator. You will be a key contributor to the team’s advocacy at the Colorado Public Utilities Commission (PUC), support its engagement on state and local legislative matters, and represent the city across a range of stakeholders. You will be a highly motivated and innovative individual with expertise in PUC advocacy and decarbonization policy, including energy efficiency, electrification, and energy systems planning. You will be a thought-leader and a clear communicator, representing the city before utilities, government staff, advocacy organizations, industry associations, and community organizations.

Specifically, as the Senior Energy Policy Advisor, you will:

Provide thought-leadership, technical expertise, and analysis on matters related to energy-, building-, and transportation-system decarbonization to develop short- and long-term energy policy initiatives and priorities.

Serve as a key contributor to Denver’s engagement in relevant regulatory proceedings at the PUC, which includes reviewing filings, drafting testimony, appearing as an expert witness, and participating in settlement negotiations with relevant parties.

Coordinate with staff from CASR and other city agencies to solicit input and incorporate feedback into CASR’s advocacy.

Serve as an expert resource across CASR disciplines by performing legislative and/or policy analysis of emerging issues or proposed policies, such as those that arise in PUC proceedings, Xcel Energy programs, state regulation, and legislation.

Develop resources and memos to brief management and leadership, including the identification of concerns, solutions to address concerns, and strategy recommendations to guide thoughtful decision-making.

Develop and deliver presentations on relevant topics across a variety of settings.

Identify opportunities to supplement Energy Program capacity with external resources, develop requests for proposals, and manage certain contracts.

Communicate and engage regularly with internal and external stakeholders, including representatives of various city agencies, community and business groups, the public, media organizations, and other stakeholders in a professional and clear manner.

Equity is a strong focus of Denver’s climate program; this position will work to ensure that the transition to clean energy services is affordable, equitable, and inclusive of under-resourced communities, low-income households, and other underrepresented and historically marginalized groups.

Other duties that may arise.

What You’ll Bring

We value diversity of ethnicity, race, socioeconomic status, sexual identity, gender, religion, language, ability, and experience and exemplify this through the makeup of our team at all levels. You'll be right at home here if you cultivate strong relationships and push yourself, your work, the people around you and Denver to the next level.

Our ideal candidate has some or all the following experience, skills, and characteristics:

Experience in energy policy with a focus on utility regulation and state utility regulatory commission practices and procedures.

Depth of technical knowledge and data analysis related to utility energy infrastructure, utility regulatory structures, and building & transportation electrification systems.

Strong project management experience with ability to push through barriers to deliver exceptional results on time.

Empathy, tact, and political savvy to identify and respond according to the internal and external politics and unique issues that impact Denver’s energy policy objectives.

An ability to influence, persuade, and negotiate with representatives from a variety of City agencies and external organizations in a collaborative manner to find mutually acceptable solutions to complex problems.

Experience incorporating the perspectives of multiple communities, including under-represented communities and historically marginalized groups in the consideration of impacts and outcomes of a decision-making process.

Willingness to grow professionally, develop innovative solutions to problems, and change processes or procedures to accomplish objectives.

Excellent written and verbal communication skills, and ability to present to diverse audiences.

Results-oriented, self-driven to contribute to a high performing team.

Willingness to take on additional responsibilities or volunteer for special projects.

Required Minimum Qualifications

Education requirement: Bachelor's Degree in a related field based on a specific position(s).

Experience Requirement: Five (5) years’ experience performing full performance professional level duties within a specialized, functional area. (This does not include clerical experience.)

Education/Experience Equivalency: One (1) year of the appropriate type and level of experience may be substituted for each required year of post-high school education.

Additional appropriate education may be substituted for the minimum experience requirements.

License/Certifications: None.

Note: While a driver’s license is not required, these positions may need to attend in-person events around Denver. The individuals must arrange for transportation to attend such events should they arise.

Application Deadline

This position is expected to stay open until Sunday, August 23, 2026. Please submit your application as soon as possible and no later than that date at 11:59 p.m. to ensure consideration.

To be considered for this position, you must include the following on your job application (upload the attachment(s) to the Resume/CV section on the My Experience tab):

Cover letter detailing your experience in decarbonization policy leadership and subject matter expertise

Resume

Executive Operations Manager

PUBLISHED: August 13, 2026

EXPIRY: September 12, 2026

Onsite

Denver, Colorado

Full Time

Executive Level Healthcare Nonprofit Charitable Organizations Operations

Summary

The Executive Operations Manager serves as a trusted strategic and operational partner to the President & CEO. This position combines sophisticated executive operations support with Board governance coordination to ensure the effectiveness of the Office of the President & CEO.

Description

Description

Colorado Hospital Association (CHA) is the leading voice of Colorado’s hospital and health system community. Representing more than 100 hospitals and health systems throughout the state, CHA serves as a trusted, credible and reliable resource on health issues, hospital data and trends for its members, media, policymakers and the general public. Through CHA, Colorado’s hospitals and health systems work together in their shared commitment to improve health and health care in Colorado. For more information on CHA, visit www.cha.com .

Position Summary:

The Executive Operations Manager serves as a trusted strategic and operational partner to the President & CEO. This position combines sophisticated executive operations support with Board governance coordination to ensure the effectiveness of the Office of the President & CEO.

This is not a traditional executive assistant role. The position anticipates needs, identifies emerging issues, and prepares decision-ready information. The successful candidate exercises exceptional judgment, discretion, and initiative, as well as awareness of the environment in which the association and CEO operate so that work can be contextualized internally and externally.

The role requires regular (4 days/week initially) in-office presence to support the President & CEO, Board and executive meetings, external relationships, and responsiveness to priorities.

This position offers meaningful exposure to health care policy and administration through close work with hospital CEOs, board members, and senior stakeholders, supporting strategic initiatives and gaining insight into association and hospital leadership.

Essential Job Duties and Responsibilities:

Strategic Executive Support

• Serve as a trusted partner and extension of the President & CEO, anticipating needs, identifying priorities, and proactively addressing issues that could affect executive effectiveness.

• Strategically manage the President & CEO's calendar, with minimal oversight, by evaluating competing requests, aligning time with priorities, resolving conflicts, and ensuring adequate preparation, travel, and decision-making time.

• Assist in the coordination and preparation of executive briefings, background materials, talking points, and correspondence for meetings, travel, speaking engagements, and external interactions.

• Independently resolve routine executive and organizational matters while exercising sound judgment regarding issues that require the President & CEO's attention.

Executive Operations Coordination

• Coordinate strategic initiatives on behalf of the President & CEO by clarifying expectations, monitoring progress, and ensuring timely follow-up.

• Coordinate Executive Leadership Team meetings, retreats, and planning sessions, including materials, logistics, decision documentation, and action-item tracking.

• Coordinate executive travel, conferences, and external meetings, including itineraries, reservations, briefing materials, and expense reporting.

• Develop and maintain efficient Executive Office systems, workflows, files, templates, and tracking tools that improve effectiveness.

Board Governance & Administration

• Manage administrative and governance details for the Board of Trustees, Executive Committee, Nominating Committee, and other assigned governing bodies.

• Prepare and distribute Board books and committee materials; maintain governance calendars, official records, minutes, resolutions, action items, and required follow-up.

• Support annual governance processes, including committee appointments, Board orientation, meeting calendars, evaluations, and other recurring governance requirements.

• Maintain trusted relationships with Board members, hospital and health system executives, the American Hospital Association, policymakers, community partners, vendors, and other external stakeholders.

• Perform other duties as assigned.

Supervisory: None

Knowledge, Skills and Experience required (unless otherwise noted):

• Bachelor’s Degree or equivalent relevant experience

• Minimum of 5 years of progressively responsible experience supporting a CEO, C-suite executive, or senior organizational leader in a complex professional environment

• Intermediate to advanced proficiency of all Microsoft Office Suite products, i.e. Teams, Outlook, Word, Excel and PowerPoint

• Demonstrated experience coordinating Board of Directors or governing body activities, including meeting materials, minutes, records, and follow-up

• Demonstrated success managing complex executive priorities, calendars, travel, confidential matters, and competing deadlines

• Strong written communication skills and experience preparing executive-level correspondence, presentations, and briefings

• Health care, hospital, membership association, nonprofit, government, or public policy experience preferred

Qualifications and Competencies:

• Exceptional judgment, discretion, and confidentiality

• Strategic thinking and strong organizational awareness

• Ability to anticipate needs and act proactively with limited direction

• Executive presence, professionalism, and political acumen

• Ability to influence, coordinate, and drive accountability without direct authority

• Strong project management, prioritization, and follow-through

• Excellent written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills

• Sound decision-making and analytical problem-solving ability

• Relationship-centered communication and diplomacy with senior stakeholders

• Adaptability, resilience, and composure in a fast-paced environment

• Meticulous attention to detail

Physical Demands / Work Environment:

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

• Working conditions are normal for a fast-paced office work environment.

• Presentation of technical material in group settings required occasionally.

• Individuals may need to sit or stand as needed.

• Occasional weekend, early morning, or evening work may be needed.

Material and Equipment Directly Used:

• CHA provided laptop with Microsoft Office 365 applications

• Virtual meeting software and hardware

• Copy machine, printer, and standard office equipment

Hiring salary range: $40-48/hour, eligible for full benefit offering

The hiring salary range represents a targeted starting salary based on candidate’s experience, education, and/or skill level. The actual starting salary may be more or less depending on individual qualifications and does not represent the position’s full salary range.

NOTE: This job description is not intended to be an exhaustive list of all duties, responsibilities, or qualifications associated with the job. The employee will be required to follow any other instructions and to perform any other duties requested by their supervisor. Nothing in this job description shall create or is intended to create, or shall be construed to constitute a contract of employment, express or implied. Employees are held accountable for all duties of this job.

Institutional Relations Manager

Salary: USD 83299.00 - 110000.00 yearly

PUBLISHED: August 13, 2026

EXPIRY: September 12, 2026

Onsite

Boulder, Colorado

Full Time

Boulder Area Development and Fundraising Nonprofit Charitable Organizations

Summary

This role identifies, cultivates, solicits, and stewards foundation and corporate funding to secure significant philanthropic support advancing UCAR's mission, while managing a portfolio of institutional donors and prospects in close collaboration with leaders across UCAR and NSF NCAR.

Description

About the Role

UCAR is excited to announce the job opening for the Manager of Institutional Relations. Reporting to the Executive Director of Friends of the National Center, this position will lead corporate and foundation fundraising efforts on behalf of UCAR. This role identifies, cultivates, solicits, and stewards foundation and corporate funding to secure significant philanthropic support advancing UCAR's mission, while managing a portfolio of institutional donors and prospects in close collaboration with leaders across UCAR and NSF NCAR.

Position details:

*Term: 2 years, with potential for extension.

*Schedule: Hybrid — 3 days/week in the Boulder office or traveling to meetings throughout the Front Range.

*Travel: Domestic travel up to 10% of time.

*Events: Availability for networking events and in-person meetings (mornings, evenings, and weekends) approximately 2–3 times per month.

Job Description

Background checks are conducted for candidates selected for hire. Learn more.

Work Location Expectations : This position is open to candidates seeking in-person or hybrid (combination of 3 days in-person and 2 days of remote), opportunities. UCAR requires ALL positions to be performed within the U.S., excluding U.S. Territories.

What You Will Do

Here is a brief summary of what one would expect to be generally responsible for in this role.

Key Responsibilities

Front-Line Fundraising & Portfolio Management

Relationship Cultivation : Initiate, build, and steward highly productive, long-term relationships with foundation program officers, foundation and corporate executives, and institutional decision-makers — designing systems to ensure donors receive exceptional reporting and impact metrics that lay the groundwork for renewed support.

Portfolio Growth : Actively manage a portfolio of ~75 active corporate and foundation prospects/donors, systematically moving them through the qualification, cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship pipeline.

Strategic Solicitations : Coordinate customized solicitation strategies to secure six- and seven-figure gifts. Manage the growth of the corporate event sponsorship program, bringing in unrestricted gifts through event sponsorships.

Prospect Research & CRM Management : Conduct prospect research to identify new or existing relationships that align with organizational funding priorities, and consistently record and track relationship development ("Moves") and institutional prospect profiles in the Salesforce database, ensuring organizational transparency and future-proofing these relationships.

Internal Collaboration

Strategic Matchmaking : Understand UCAR and NSF NCAR's organizational capabilities and emerging initiatives well enough to connect them with aligned funders — either by matching an internal project to a target foundation, or identifying a foundation's strategic goals and working internally to surface the strongest project to move forward. Serve as the central liaison between corporations/foundations and internal technical teams, ensuring fundraising strategies align with scientific integrity and organizational capacity.

Proposal Strategy & Stewardship

Concept Development : Support the strategic framing of pitches and letters of inquiry (LOIs), determining how a project should be positioned to win corporate or foundation support.

Preferred Qualifications

Education and Experience

Bachelor’s degree required (Master’s degree preferred);

5 years of relevant program experience;

Or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

Minimum of 5 years of successful fundraising experience, with a proven track record of securing significant gifts from corporate and foundation entities.

Experience navigating complex non-profit, academic, scientific, or highly matrixed research environments.

Demonstrated ability to "open doors," navigate institutional hierarchies, and build authentic rapport with external decision-makers.

Exceptional verbal presentation skills, including the ability to translate complex Earth system science, computational modeling, and educational concepts into accessible, compelling value propositions for diverse foundation audiences.

Exceptional emotional intelligence and a proven ability to work productively with subject matter experts, administrative leads, and development staff.

Demonstrated ability to work independently, set priorities, and manage competing tasks and deadlines with strong attention to detail and flexibility in the face of change.

Skill in identifying specific, measurable, achievable, relevant, and time-bound goals and opportunities.

Advanced skills in word processing, spreadsheets, and presentations (Word, PowerPoint, Excel, and Google suite or similar software).

Ability to use discretion in handling confidential information.

Experience with non-profit CRM databases, ideally Salesforce.

REQUIRED APPLICATION MATERIALS (preferably in PDF Format) :

Resume

Cover Letter

In lieu of a traditional cover letter, answer the following prompts that address the critical skills needed for this position. Your answers will be read and weighed equally to your Resume/CV and should provide specific, detailed, and informative responses based on your direct and previous work experiences. Please keep responses to 1-3 paragraphs per prompt.

Track record with significant gifts

Describe a corporate or foundation gift (six- or seven-figures, if possible) that you personally cultivated from first contact through to close. What was your strategy for moving that funder through the pipeline, and what specifically made your solicitation approach successful?

Translating technical work into funder priorities

Tell us about a time you had to connect a complex, technical, or scientific initiative with an external funder's priorities (either by finding the right funder for an existing project, or by working internally) to identify a project that matched a funder's goals. How did you build that bridge, and what was the outcome?

Navigating complex/matrixed organizations

This role requires building trust with both external funders and internal scientists, program directors, and leadership across two organizations (UCAR and NSF NCAR). Describe your experience working within a complex, academic, or highly matrixed environment. How did you earn credibility with technical experts while also managing external relationships, and what did you do when their priorities didn't initially align?

Application Requirements

Cover Letter, Resume/CV

For full consideration, all application materials must be submitted by 12am (MST) at the start of the application deadline . These should highlight how your skills and experiences align with the responsibilities of this position. We recognize that no candidate will meet 100% of the listed qualifications. If you believe your background has prepared you for success in this role, we encourage you to apply.

Supplemental questionnaires are often requested in lieu of a cover letter, where you address critical skills needed for the position. Your answers will be read and weighed equally to your resume and should provide specific, detailed, and informative responses based on your direct and previous work experiences.

Background checks and/or federal screenings are conducted for candidates selected for hire.

Benefits Overview

UCAR offers a comprehensive benefits package : health insurance, dental, retirement plan, leave plans, tuition assistance, and employee assistance programs:

Medical, Dental, Vision, and Short & Long Term Disability Insurance

Generous retirement plan – UCAR contributes of 10% of base salary

Time Off Plans

Minimum 20 days of annual PTO

10 paid holidays

12 weeks of paid parental leave

FAMLI Leave

Tuition Assistance Program

Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF) eligible employer

UCAR is an Equal Opportunity Employer and welcomes applications from all individuals. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, age, sex, gender identity, disability, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law. Applicants are not required to provide age-related information (like date of birth or graduation dates) in initial submissions.

For sponsored positions : UCAR can sponsor individuals for H-1B status only if they are already in the U.S. in H-1B status or another visa status that allows them to change to H-1B status within the U.S. UCAR is unable to sponsor new H-1B visas for individuals who are outside the U.S. and need to obtain H-1B status through Consular Processing.

While UCAR does not prohibit the use of AI tools in job applications, we strongly recommend that applicants submit primarily original work.

All roles require compliance with U.S. export control regulations and work location requirements. All hybrid staff are expected to work on-site approximately 3 days per week.

RFQ: Park Hill Park Design

Closed

August 13, 2026, 02:00 PM

Reference number Solicitation No. 202684823

Status Pending

Solicitation No. 202684823
June 30, 2026

The Denver Bond Office (“DBO”) and the Department of Transportation & Infrastructure (“DOTI”), City and County of Denver (“City”), has issued a Request for Qualifications (the “RFQ”) for Park Hill Park Architectural & Engineering Design Services. RFQ documents will be available for download at www.bidnetdirect.com/cityandcountyofdenverdoti .

General Statement of Work: Since at least 2018, neighbors have wondered what the future of the Park Hill Golf Club might be. Several different planning efforts or development proposals have engaged residents since that time, and in 2025, after the City of Denver purchased the land, Denver Parks and Recreation (“DPR”) launched a park visioning process. This process aimed to work with the community to develop a high-level vision framework of the important values, amenities, opportunities, and “bones” of the future park – the “big idea” to guide future design and construction phases.

Work will generally include construction documents for demolition and site preparation; earthwork; drainage/channel improvements; site electrical including lighting, Ultraviolet (UV) treatment, and pumping system for water play area; paving & small pedestrian bridges; walls & boulders; site amenities; ecological and habitat educational features; shade structures; landscaping, including seeding, sodding, and native plantings; irrigation; irrigation pump station; outdoor adventure and playgrounds; and the potential to include 2- years of landscape-establishment.

Vibrant Denver Bond Program : Approved by voters in 2025, the $950 million Vibrant Denver Bond Program is delivering 58 major projects across Denver, including libraries, parks and recreation centers, cultural facilities, affordable housing, improved streets and bridges, a family health clinic, a children’s advocacy center, and much more – without adding any new taxes. This bond program was informed by direct community input from thousands of Denverites and community leaders. The City will build the projects in this bond over six years from 2026 – 2031.

RFQ: Boettcher Concert Hall Renovation

RFQ: Boettcher Concert Hall Renovation

Closed

July 21, 2026, 02:00 PM

Reference number Solicitation No. 202684561

Status Awarded

Summary The City seeks qualified design teams for renovating Boettcher Concert Hall, including major system replacements, interior upgrades, acoustics, seating, lighting, AV, tech, circulation, ADA improvements, and necessary exterior work. Design must also incorporate youth education spaces.

Winning entity
DAVID OWEN TRYBA ARCHITECTS, A PROFESSIONAL CORPORATION (Tryba Architects)

Date awarded August 13, 2026

Solicitation No. 202684561
June 1, 2026

The Denver Bond Office (“DBO”) and the Department of Transportation & Infrastructure (“DOTI”), City and County of Denver (“City”), has issued a Request for Qualifications (the “RFQ”) for Boettcher Concert Hall Renovation Architectural & Engineering Design Services. RFQ documents will be available for download at www.bidnetdirect.com/cityandcountyofdenverdoti .

General Statement of Work: This project will renovate and rehabilitate the existing Boettcher Concert Hall on the Denver Performing Arts Complex at 1000 14th St, Denver, CO 80202. The renovation will include critical repairs, system upgrades, and address program needs.

The Boettcher Concert Hall Project will renovate the existing facility to address building systems and finishes that have exceeded their useful life. The project scope includes upgrades to HVAC, fire protection, life safety, data, technology, stage lighting, and audiovisual systems, along with new interior finishes, seating, and acoustic improvements. Floor plan modifications will improve circulation, operational functionality, ADA compliance, and integrate an education component. Exterior improvements, including roofing and façade repairs or replacement, will be included as required. The project will also evaluate and design a pavilion expansion for patron use, along with a west-side addition intended to activate the adjacent sculpture park.

Vibrant Denver Bond Program : Approved by voters in 2025, the $950 million Vibrant Denver Bond Program is delivering 58 major projects across Denver, including libraries, parks and recreation centers, cultural facilities, affordable housing, improved streets and bridges, a family health clinic, a children’s advocacy center, and much more – without adding any new taxes. This bond program was informed by direct community input from thousands of Denverites and community leaders. The City will build the projects in this bond over six years from 2026 – 2031.

A Pre-Submittal Meeting will be held on June 9, 2026, at 8:00 a.m., local time. ( Meeting Agenda (PDF, 45KB) ) To access the meeting, please call 720-388-6219 and enter the conference ID: 223 209 119# or join via Microsoft Teams . Consultants are responsible for any information conveyed at this meeting.

**Optional Site Visit: An optional site visit will be held on June 10, 2026, 10:00 a.m. – 12:00 p.m. , local time . Please RSVP and the site visit details will be sent via email.

Questions Deadline: June 29, 2026, at 2:00 p.m., local time.

Submittals will only be received via the online electronic bid service through BidNet . Submittals are due at 2:00 p.m. on July 21, 2026 . Late submissions will not be accepted.

MWBE Participation Goal: 19%

Contract Administrator: Michele Foust, DOTI.Procurement@denvergov.org

Minimum Wage: City contracts are subject to payment of City Minimum Wage established pursuant to Section 20-82 through 20-84 DRMC.

General: As the City’s best interests may appear, the City Engineer reserves the right to waive informalities in, and to reject any or all proposals.

Publication Dates: June 1, 2026

Summary Jurassic Lot Improvements

General Statement of Work
The Red Rocks Amphitheatre Jurassic Lot Improvements project consists of all site-enabling and horizontal infrastructure work necessary to prepare the site for future development and operational use. The work generally includes demolition and site preparation; mass earthwork, grading, and erosion control; construction of storm drainage infrastructure, culverts, drainage conveyance systems, and associated appurtenances; installation and extension of electrical distribution systems, site power, lighting infrastructure, and related utility improvements; roadway and parking area subgrade preparation; and all associated utility coordination, traffic control, and restoration required to establish a fully functional site platform. The intent of this phase is to deliver the complete civil, grading, stormwater, and electrical backbone infrastructure required to support future improvements while maintaining site access and operational considerations. Hardscape improvements, including but not limited to curb and gutter, site concrete, decorative concrete paving, and asphalt paving , shall be excluded from the Base Bid and carried separately by all bidders as identified Add Alternates for potential inclusion at the Owner’s discretion following bid evaluation. Additional work will be required around landscaping, site furnishings, and preparation for a future Restroom Building.

To access the meeting, please join via Microsoft Teams .

Questions Deadline: August 28, 2026 at 3:00 p.m. local time.

Bids will be received and accepted by M.A. Mortenson via SmartBid .

Plans Available via SmartBid .

Each bidder must have submitted a prequalification application a minimum of ten (10) calendar days prior to the response due date. Applications must be submitted via B2Gnow . To view the Rules and information on how to apply, please visit our website at www.denvergov.org/prequalification . If you have prequalification questions, please reach out to DOTI.Prequal@denvergov.org .

Status Awarded

Summary Contractor must maintain, inspect, test, and replace all non-structural traffic signal components, ensuring proper operation of controllers, wiring, indications, detection, preemption, communication, timing, backup power, and luminaires, and verify all equipment, structures, and cabinets are in good condition.

Winning entity
Lumin8 Transportation Technologies, LLC

Value $985,000.00

Date awarded June 24, 2026

Contract No. 202684240 – Traffic Signals Preventative Maintenance CDOT Intersections
May 5, 2026

General Statement of Work
The contractor will be responsible for all routine maintenance, periodic inspection and/or testing, and replacement of all non-structural traffic signal components. This includes, but is not limited to, cabinet components, controllers, wiring, signal indications, detection equipment, pedestrian push buttons, pole mounted signs, software, licenses, firmware, and communication devices to keep the signal operational as described herein. The Conflict Monitor should be tested and operating correctly. Verify each signal head is in good condition and the backplate is attached and in good condition. Verify each signal lens is operating and visibled. Verify detection is working and is detecting vehicles, motorcycles, bicycles, and pedestrians if applicable. Verify preemption is properly operating. Verify the structure is in good condition, free from cracks and rust, visible portions of the caissons are free from cracks. Verify Signal Timing is operating as programmed. Verify Controller and Cabinet are clean and in good repair. Verify communication to signal is connected and operating, where applicable. Verify backup power is tested for proper operation, where applicable. Verify all luminaries attached to the signal are operating, where applicable. This is a Maximum Value hard bid contract. The maximum contract amount is $985,000.00.

Tower Road Sanitary Interceptor Phase 1

Tower Road Sanitary Interceptor Phase 1

Closed

August 04, 2026, 02:00 PM

Reference number Contract No. 202684690

Status Pending

Summary Phase 1 rehabilitates the Tower Road Sanitary Sewer Interceptor from 59th to 68th Ave, including eight point repairs and 5,974 feet of cured in place (CIPP) lining. Work involves excavations up to 30 feet, manhole and pipe replacement, traffic control, and bypass pumping.

Contract No. 202684690 – Tower Road Sanitary Interceptor – Phase 1
June 9, 2026

General Statement of Work
This project is Phase 1 of the rehabilitation of the Tower Road Sanitary Sewer Interceptor. Phase 1 extends from 59th Avenue to 68th Avenue. This phase includes eight (8) point repairs and 5,974 feet of cured in place pipe lining. The point repairs will include excavations to approximately 30 feet and replacing manholes and pipe. Associated required work will include traffic control and bypass pumping.

Peoria Street HSIP 23 Vision Zero Project

Peoria Street HSIP 23 Vision Zero Project

Closed

July 23, 2026, 01:00 PM

Reference number Contract No. 202684820

Status Pending

Summary Construction of safety improvements at three Montbello intersections: Peoria/44th (median modification and partial signal), Peoria/46th (new signal, ADA and sidewalk/median work), and 47th/Paris (widening and raised median with right-in/right-out restrictions).

Contract No. 202684820 – Peoria Street HSIP 23 Vision Zero Project
June 15, 2026

General Statement of Work
Construction of safety related signal and median improvements at three intersections in the Montbello neighborhood on Peoria Street at 44th, 46th, and on 47th Avenue just west of Peoria at Paris Street. At, Peoria St and 44th Ave - Modify the raised-curb median to restrict eastbound left-turn vehicle movements and install a partial signal that would allow for protected northbound left-turn movements. At, Peoria St and 46th Ave - Install a new (standard) traffic signal and related improvements to ADA ramps, sidewalk and median removal. At, 47th Ave and Paris St - Widen 47th Avenue in the vicinity of Paris Street and provide a raised-curb median to restrict southbound Paris Street to right-in right-out and to restrict left-turns from 47th Avenue to Paris Street.

This project is part of the 2021 RISE Denver Bond Program , which is a 10-year, $260 million general obligation bond program approved by voters in 2021. The program will drive economic recovery by creating thousands of jobs, investing in local businesses, and bringing critical infrastructure and community assets to historically underserved areas of the city. Through four different categories of infrastructure projects, RISE Denver will serve our most vulnerable residents and unhoused neighbors, increase mobility and safety in our neighborhoods and accessibility within city facilities, and preserve Denver’s history and culture through building restorations. More information can be found on the City’s RISE Denver website .

RFP: Colfax Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) Custodial & Snow Removal Services

RFP: Colfax Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) Custodial & Snow Removal Services

Closed

July 09, 2026, 10:00 AM

Reference number Solicitation No. 202684627

Status Pending

Solicitation No.202684627
June 8, 2026

The Department of Transportation & Infrastructure (“DOTI”), City and County of Denver (“City”), has issued a Request for Proposals (the “RFP”) for Custodial and Snow Removal Services for Colfax BRT. RFP documents will be available for download at www.bidnetdirect.com/cityandcountyofdenverdoti .

General Statement of Work: Provide custodial services for fourteen (14) BRT stations between Pennsylvania Street and Colorado Boulevard. These services shall include daily station cleaning and trash removal, monthly power washing, on-call services for specific incident clean up, and snow/ice removal during snow events. Services are expected to start in September 2026 and run through December 2027.

A Pre-Proposal Meeting will be held on June 15, 2026, at 1:00 p.m. local time. To access the meeting, please call 720-388-6219 and enter the conference ID: 685 928 001# or join via Microsoft Teams . Contractors are responsible for any information conveyed at this meeting.

Questions Deadline: June 25, 2026, at 10:00 a.m. local time.

Proposals will only be received via the online electronic bid service through BidNet . Proposals are due at 10:00 a.m. on July 9 , 2026 . Late submissions will not be accepted.

DSBO Goal: No Program

Contract Administrator: Micaela Martinez, DOTI.Procurement@denvergov.org

Prevailing Wage and Minimum Wage: Contracts for construction, reconstruction, and remodeling are subject to the City prevailing wage rate requirements established pursuant to Section 20-76, DRMC. City contracts are subject to payment of City Minimum Wage established pursuant to Section 20-82 through 20-84 DRMC.

General: As the City’s best interests may appear, the Executive Director of Transportation and Infrastructure (DOTI) reserves the right to waive informalities in, and to reject any or all proposals.

RRIC Construction Services for 2026 Offseason Work – Bid Package 1

RRIC Construction Services for 2026 Offseason Work – Bid Package 1

Closing date

September 08, 2026, 03:00 PM

Reference number Contract No. 202577784

Status Open

Summary Supply Hub, Backstage Access Gate, and North & South Stage Tower Stair Refurbishment

General Statement of Work

Supply Hub:

The Supply Hub Building is a new approximately 248-square-foot accessory storage facility adjacent to the existing Red Rocks Visitor Center designed by Studiotrope Design Collective. The scope of work includes site preparation and selective demolition; construction of reinforced concrete foundations, CMU masonry walls, structural steel framing, and metal roof deck; installation of a green roof system with integrated irrigation and native plantings; and full integration of architectural, structural, civil, landscape, mechanical, plumbing, electrical, and technology systems. The project is designed as a Type IIA, fully sprinklered structure supporting Assembly (A-2) occupancy with accessory storage (S-1), and incorporates durable exterior materials, ADA-compliant design, and modern building systems including lighting, ventilation, and access control. Work must be carefully coordinated with existing site utilities and operations, as the facility will remain open to the public throughout construction. Bidders are responsible for providing all labor, materials, equipment, and supervision necessary to complete the project in accordance with the IFC Documents, and all applicable codes and regulations.

Backstage Access Gate:

Designed by Short Elliot Hendrickson, Inc., the Backstage Access Gate project consists of demolition of existing gate infrastructure and asphalt improvements, followed by installation of a new controlled-access entry system including traffic barrier arms, gate access control equipment, RFID/badge reader systems, and associated electrical infrastructure. The work includes construction of concrete foundations and pads, installation of steel bollards and posts, curb and gutter modifications, and coordination with existing site features such as utilities, drainage structures, and adjacent facilities. Electrical scope includes new equipment, backup battery panels, conduit, and integration with existing power and communications systems to support automated gate operations. The project requires careful site coordination, traffic control, and maintenance of operations within an active Red Rocks Amphitheatre environment. Bidders shall provide all labor, materials, equipment, and supervision necessary to complete the work in accordance with the IFC Documents, and all applicable federal, state, and local regulations and permitting requirements.

North & South Tower Stair Refurbishment:

Designed by Short Elliott Hendrickson, Inc., the Red Rocks Amphitheatre North & South Tower Stair Replacement Project consists of demolition of existing stair systems and installation of new structural steel stairs, landings, railings, and guardrails serving the stage and backstage areas of Red Rocks Amphitheatre. Work includes replacement of stair stringers, treads, platforms, and support steel; restoration of select existing railings and gates; concrete repairs; application of protective coatings and waterproofing systems; and installation of slip-resistant finishes on all new walking surfaces.

The project also includes limited electrical work associated with removal and replacement of existing handrail lighting, new conduit and junction boxes, and coordination with existing electrical systems. As the work occurs within a designated historic landmark, contractors shall preserve existing stair geometry, protect historic features and exposed rock formations, and coordinate construction activities to minimize impacts to ongoing amphitheater operations. Bidders shall provide all labor, materials, equipment, supervision, permits, and incidentals necessary to complete the work in accordance with the 100% Construction Documents and all applicable federal, state, and local requirements.
